text:
King's College London is a member institution and was a founding college of the federal University of London. It is part of the "golden triangle" of research universities in London, alongside Imperial College London, the London School of Economics, and University College London. The college is also part of King's Health Partners and was a founding member of the Francis Crick Institute.
King's College London operates across five central London campuses: the Strand Campus (which houses the arts and science faculties), the Waterloo Campus, St. Thomas' Campus in Lambeth, the Guy's Campus near London Bridge, and the Denmark Hill Campus in Southwark. Its academic structure includes nine faculties, such as Life Sciences and Medicine, the Dickson Poon School of Law, and the Florence Nightingale Faculty of Nursing, Midwifery and Palliative Care. The institution has secured independent degree-awarding powers and is recognized for its research income and rankings.
